chunks: They will answer: 'Glory to You. It was not worthy of us to seek any protector other than You. But You allowed them and their fathers a life of ease until they turned oblivious of the Reminder. They were a people impenitent.'

key_terms.الذِّكْرَ: The Reminder (referring to God or the Quran)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَکَ: Glory to You (an expression of divine perfection)

ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers choose their false gods according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Furqan illustrates the ultimate confession of the polytheists, who attribute their spiritual blindness not to a lack of divine proof, but to the 'enjoyment' (mataa) God granted them, which lulled them into negligence. This highlights the concept of 'tadhalluk' (attachment) to worldly ease as a primary cause for forgetting the Reminder (Al-Dhikr), a theme central to the struggle between material comfort and spiritual awareness. The verse serves as a warning that prosperity, when unaccompanied by mindfulness, can lead to total ruin (bur).
